requirement: A command says which scenarios a change touched
scenario: The terminal form of the lines that prove nothing carries them
note: The claim says the changed line comes back 'as written', but renderUnmatched (src/cli/render.ts:265) calls .trim() on the source before embedding it in the text form, while the JSON form keeps it untrimmed. The fixture's changed line ('export const helper = 2') has no leading/trailing whitespace, so trim() is a no-op and the test can't tell verbatim rendering from trimmed rendering. A changed line with real indentation would lose it in the text form, contradicting 'as written' and the requirement's own promise that the terminal form says the same thing as the JSON one.

requirement: A command says which scenarios a change touched
scenario: Requirements come back in capability then requirement order
note: The fixture comment claims dropping either half of the sort (capability, or the requirement tie-break) moves zeta off the end and fails the test. Verified by mutation: dropping the capability key (sorting by requirement text alone) still sorts correctly and the test passes, because the requirement strings happen to alphabetize into the same order (first < second < zeta). Dropping the requirement tie-break instead does fail the test, but zeta stays last -- it's the two alpha requirements that swap places, not zeta moving off the end. The comment misdescribes what each mutation actually does.
